automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.policy: Only sources published or visibly updated within the last 7 days; ambiguous, future, missing, and boundary-only dates excluded.

excluded_candidates.reason: Topically relevant, but no clear page-visible publication or update date found in opened source.
Topically relevant docs for PR outputs, but opened page showed no visible publication or update date.

federation_routing: Broad ecosystem entity updates are upstream-owned by the AI wiki; this artifact preserves only local practice, workflow, governance, verification, adoption, and implementation implications.
follow_up_notes: Do not update docs/wiki directly from this watcher artifact; route through normal raw-source ingest.
Verify search-result-only dates for TrueFoundry, A4BEE, and GoGloby during ingest before using them as strict-window evidence.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub described Copilot sessions in Slack and Microsoft Teams where shared conversations can plan, investigate, and hand off coding-agent work; Teams write access gates who can trigger code changes. Public reporting on Slack Code adds shared project channels, live previews, feedback, approvals, agent tabs, and existing Slack admin controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should check whether shared-channel pages need stronger language about channel-visible approvals, write-access gating, and admin-control evidence.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Reinforces the local rule that shared chat is a coordination and evidence surface, while repository permission, approval, billing, and audit boundaries remain separate authority gates.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TrueFoundry frames agent governance as a graph problem where designed architecture and executed graph differ; execution evidence comes from harness events, gateway traces, IAM records, and downstream logs. It also names MCP tools, skills, sandboxing, human checkpoints, context management, and session state as execution-loop components.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route broad product coverage upstream; keep local implications around graph execution evidence, skills, context packages, and checkpoints.
qualifying_updates.published_or_updated: search result visible date: 2 days before 2026-08-24 run
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports edge-level authorization and artifact-boundary practice: diagrams and tool reachability are insufficient without executed-edge evidence and separately governed skills, tools, checkpoints, and state.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Express Computer argues that approved AI applications can become shadow AI when identity, feature set, integrations, data, purpose, or action capability changes inside ordinary workflows, including browser extensions, plug-ins, connectors, MCP servers, and embedded assistants.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should consider adding interaction-state checks to browser-runtime and sensitive-data control leaves.
named_entities: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Strengthens local practice that governance must follow interaction state, data path, identity, connectors, and agent actions rather than static app approval.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar argues policies alone cannot govern AI systems that access data, applications, identities, infrastructure, and operational workflows; it recommends continuous capability identification, inherited-permission review, and business-impact-based controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep the local lens on operational governance controls and inherited permission review.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Reinforces that approval boundaries and edge authorization require operational control evidence, not only written acceptable-use policy.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar argues AI-generated and AI-carried code needs behavior-policy checks before execution, because source, signature, or SBOM-style provenance can miss malicious runtime behavior.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest should avoid duplicating broad AI-malware coverage and focus on execution-policy gates for local generated-code workflows.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Adds a local acceptance-gate implication: generated code and refactoring outputs need behavior and execution-policy evidence, not only provenance or static prechecks.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: A public AI-generated code review policy post proposes risk tiers, human approval rules, security gates, and cost math for AI-generated changes.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: If ingested, cite as practice evidence rather than as authoritative industry standard.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports local review practice around risk-tiered review, explicit human approval, security gates, and review-cost accounting for AI-generated code.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: A4BEE ties the EU AI Act high-risk enforcement date to agents that take actions in regulated settings, emphasizing that action-taking systems need designed governance rather than answer-only oversight.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Treat as routing evidence for high-risk action gates; verify primary regulatory citations during ingest.
qualifying_updates.published_or_updated: search result visible date: 5 days before 2026-08-24 run
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Reinforces local approval and acceptance-gate practice for regulated agent actions, while broad EU AI Act background remains upstream-owned.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GoGloby describes AI code refactoring as agent-assisted improvement of internal structure without behavior changes, targeting duplication, naming, oversized functions, dead dependencies, and module boundaries.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Verify page-visible publication date during ingest before treating it as strict-window evidence.
